learning_outcomes.text: Choose and apply the most appropriate methods and techniques to analyze and solve problems defined by data that represent a challenge due to their volume, velocity, variety, or heterogeneity, including computational, mathematical, statistical, and signal processing methods.

Have the experimental and analytical skills to work autonomously, being able to plan experiments and describe, analyze, evaluate, and interpret the resulting information to propose alternative and novel solutions to known and/or emerging problems.
Create models and make decisions based on available data, combining acquired knowledge and being able to apply new knowledge to problem-solving.
Ability to integrate into a multidisciplinary team within the framework of a data science project.
Ability to access and manage information in different formats for later analysis with the aim of obtaining knowledge from data.
Ability to express data processing results clearly and convincingly both in writing and orally.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their area of study.

That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
That students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Understand the characteristics and functionality of database management systems, particularly those most suitable for managing large volumes of data, in order to apply this knowledge in the construction of intelligent systems.
Manage databases to store and extract information: Relational databases and data modeling.
Understand the basic concepts of different non-relational database models and technologies (document, column family, graph, etc.).
Use the corresponding languages (SQL, CQL, APIs, etc.) to update and extract information from databases from applications.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and structure of Database Management Systems.
T1: Architecture and functionality of Database Management Systems.
Conceptual design with the Entity-Relationship model, integrity constraints.
Relational databases: relational model, transactions, security and concurrency control, data languages (definition, modification, and query).
T3: Relational databases. Relational Model. Relational Algebra and Calculus.
T4: Design and optimization of relational databases. Normalization and query optimization.
T5: Transactions, security and concurrency control.
P1. Creation, manipulation and querying of databases. Procedures and functions. Packages. Exceptions. Implementation of semantic constraints.
P2. Use of libraries for data access.
Non-relational databases: Basic characteristics, storage types. Graph, document, semantic databases (RDF, OWL). Technologies for handling non-relational databases.
T6: Advanced databases. Data warehouses and multidimensional modeling.
P3. Creation, manipulation and querying of non-relational databases.

assessment_methods.method: Attendance / participation in seminars and tutorials (includes online) (AP)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum of 5 out of 10 points must be achieved in Theoretical Exams (P1) and Practical Exams (P2). If these minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as: 0.4 * P1 + 0.45 * P2 + 0.1 * P3 + 0.05 * P4. If the minimums for P1 or P2 are not met, the final grade will be the minimum of 4 points out of 10 and the weighted average. To pass, the final grade must be at least 5 out of 10. For extraordinary calls, the evaluation consists of Theoretical Exams (P1) (50%) and Practical Exams (P2) (50%), both requiring a minimum of 5 out of 10. Grades from the ordinary call with 5 or more points are carried over.
